attorneys.name: Olivia Mooney
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
I am originally from Georgia and have spent most of my life in Atlanta. In 2007, I graduated from Agnes Scott College with a B.A. in International Relations and German. I worked as a paralegal for 5 years, helping employees who were wrongly terminated due to discrimination and/or retaliation. In 2015, I received my J.D. from Georgia State University. While in law school, I clerked for the Honorable Vincent Hill at the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. I also had the opportunity to volunteer at Central Outreach and Advocacy Center in Atlanta, assisting unhoused individuals in obtaining housing, healthcare, and identification.

My work before and during law school solidified my goal of helping people when they need it most. After law school, I represented individuals in Chapter 7 and 13 bankruptcies before joining a large insurance defense firm. While at my previous firm, I helped create and implement a bankruptcy and insolvency department. After a few years of defending insurance companies, I came to my senses and remembered why I wanted to practice law. I joined Parnall Law Firm, LLC because I want to represent those in need.

After years of living hours away from nature, I am excited for all the outdoor activities New Mexico has to offer. In my free time, I enjoy hiking, camping, yoga, and skiing (though not very well). I have a poorly trained mutt, Sassafras, that rules the house.

attorneys.name: Brian J. Murray
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised on Long Island, New York, the youngest of three. Grew up camping with the family and playing all kinds of sports, particularly hockey, football, and lacrosse. Played Rugby at Boston College, MA where I earned a B.A. in Political Science and Philosophy in 1999. Following graduation, I returned to Long Island and obtained my J.D. from Hofstra University Law School, in 2002 and passed the New York State Bar later that year. At my first legal job, I worked for a firm specializing in Insurance Defense Litigation, which enabled me to gain experience at trying cases. From there I went on to work as in-house counsel for insurance carriers at Geico, Progressive, and Plymouth Rock Assurance, as well as a trial firm for various other carriers. I earned a reputation as being a successful trial attorney, which led to management opportunities. I gained a reputation as being a successful trial attorney, which led to management opportunities.

When I graduated college and began Law School, I joined my hometown volunteer Fire Department. As an active member, I found great joy in giving back to my community and helping those around me. I have looked to do the same in my professional career.

My wife and I married in 2005 and lived on Long Island our entire lives. During the pandemic, my family and I decided we were ready for a new adventure which led us to Albuquerque, New Mexico, and the Parnall Law Firm, LLC. I am joining Parnall Law Firm, LLC at the perfect time in my career. After working for Insurance Companies for over 18 years, I finally can get back to helping people in my community; fighting for justice for injured victims, is exactly what I was looking for at this stage in my career.

attorneys.name: Jonas Nahoum
attorneys.practice_type: Transactional Law Lawyers in Santa Fe, NM
attorneys.bio: Upon graduating magna cum laude from Hastings College of the Law in San Francisco in 2003, Mr. Nahoum served as a federal law clerk to the Honorable D. Lowell Jensen of the United States District Court for the Northern District of California. As a federal clerk, Mr. Nahoum faced a broad range of duties including conducting legal research, preparing bench memos, drafting orders and opinions, proofreading the judge’s orders and opinions, verifying citations, communicating with counsel regarding case management and procedural requirements, and assisting the judge during courtroom proceedings. Upon completing his clerkship, Mr. Nahoum served as a litigation associate at one of San Francisco’s top law firms, Howard Rice Nemerovski Canady Falk & Rabkin (currently Arnold & Porter), for four years, representing clients in matters involving attorney professional responsibility and ethics, business and banking law, white collar criminal defense, and appeals before the California Supreme Court and Court of Appeals. After moving to Santa Fe in 2009, Mr. Nahoum represented borrowers in foreclosure during the height of the housing crisis that affected New Mexico homeowners from 2010 through 2013. Currently, Mr. Nahoum’s practice encompasses both transactional and litigation matters, representing New Mexico public entities in public finance, insurance defense, utility issues, and civil rights and other constitutional issues. Mr. Nahoum has two sons, lives in Santa Fe, and is an avid guitar player, hiker, skier, and off-road tri-athlete.

attorneys.bio:
Carlos A. Obrey-Espinoza joined Lerner and Rowe’s New Mexico legal team in 2020. He has successfully won over 30 jury trials since 2007.

Prior to representing Albuquerque personal injury clients at Lerner and Rowe Injury Attorneys, he spent 17 years learning the ins and outs of the insurance industry, serving as an attorney for insurance carriers. In 2018, he shifted his focus from representing insurance companies to upholding accident injury victims’ rights through plaintiff personal injury work.

Mr. Obrey-Espinoza believes that the most important parts of practicing law are always doing what is in the best interests of the client and never compromising your ethical or professional duties.

Educational and Professional Background

Mr. Obrey-Espinoza grew up on a horse ranch in Northern New Mexico and graduated from Los Alamos High School. He received a Bachelor of Arts in English Literature and Psychology with Honors from New Mexico State University in 1991. A few years later he was drawn to the legal field and earned his law degree from the University of New Mexico School of Law in 2001.

He is a member of the New Mexico Bar and has a Distinguished Rating from Martindale-Hubbell for Ethical Standards.

More about Carlos Obrey-Espinoza

Mr. Obrey-Espinoza has lived in Albuquerque since 1996. When he isn’t looking out for the welfare of his clients, he enjoys watching films, singing off-key to 80s music, and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: Bertrand Russell Parnall
attorneys.practice_type: Bicycle and Pedestrian Accidents Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Ever since launching Parnall Law in 2009, Bert Parnall has focused on trying to make lives better for people who have been injured through no fault of their own. Parnall spent his childhood in remote parts of the world, which provided valuable early experience that helped to create the lawyer he is today. While pursuing a major in history and French at Rice University in the early 1990s, he spent a year studying at La Sorbonne in Paris. After receiving his undergraduate degree, Parnall attended the University of Mexico School of Law. Parnall spent four years as a prosecutor in the most violent county in New Mexico. His work there provided a sense of satisfaction that he was helping to make lives better for crime victims, but he wanted to have a more direct hand in working for crime victims and injury victims and decided to move into personal injury plaintiff’s work. Even with a busy law firm to run Bert has spent time giving back to the community through the Rotary Club of Albuquerque, Albuquerque Public Schools Foundation, Popejoy, Make a Wish Foundation and his partnership with Mothers Against Drunk Driving.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal and Civil Defense Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Nathan Pederson is a dedicated attorney with a rich background in criminal and civil defense. Born in Wisconsin and raised in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Nathan brings deep community ties to his practice. Nathan graduated from the University of New Mexico with a Bachelor of Business Administration prior to attending the University of New Mexico School of Law.

Prior to joining Jones Law Firm, Nathan most recently ran his own law office representing clients in a wide array of legal arenas. Nathan’s passion is representing clients facing criminal charges.

As a young lawyer Nathan learned the art of defending clients facing DWI and other traffic related charges. Nathan traveled the state presenting to criminal defense attorneys on new innovative ways to defend against a DWI charge. Nathan prides himself in being a fierce yet empathetic fighter who is dedicated to protecting the rights of his clients.

Away from work Nathan enjoys getting outside and exploring the beauty of New Mexico. Nathan along with his wife love to travel around our state embracing the culture and history that is abundant. Nathan is an avid golfer that tries to hit the links whenever possible. But for your case, he would be a much better golfer.

attorneys.bio:
I am a lifelong New Mexican, born and raised in Albuquerque. I graduated from Sandia High School and earned my B.A. in Political Science from the University of New Mexico, where I later attended the UNM School of Law. During law school, I was elected by my peers to serve as Student Bar Association President and competed on the school’s ABA Negotiation Team. Outside of work, I recently married my best friend, and we enjoy life with our two cats, Lux and Ponyo. I love spending time at home reading fantasy novels, watching anime, and playing the Nintendo Switch. On weekends, I enjoy exploring the local markets or discovering new local coffee spots around Albuquerque. Last, I am a red chile lover.

attorneys.name: Lydia Pizzonia
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation - Plaintiff Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
I am originally from Amarillo, Texas, but moved to Albuquerque in 1989. I graduated Magna Cum Laude from UNM School of Law in 2019. Prior to attending law school, I graduated from Adams State University with a BSBA in finance. Between undergrad and law school, I had the privilege of staying home with our three children while Justin practiced law.

After watching Justin change the lives of countless injured workers for a number of years, I was inspired to study law so that I could effect change in the same way. While in law school, I received a clerkship at the United States District Court for the District of New Mexico. I also worked in the UNM law clinic where I practiced Indian Law, focusing on civil rights violations and consumer law. I received the "Outstanding Clinical Student Award" from The Clinical Legal Education Association in part due to a successful outcome from a wrongful conviction case, as well as for my work exposing unfair trade practices within the rent-to-own industry.

I have worked with Justin since 2014 as CFO for Pizzonia Law. Over those years, Justin taught me what it means to practice law aggressively, but with compassion and integrity. I look forward to helping clients change their lives for the better, in the same way Justin has helped so many since 2009.

attorneys.name: Justin P. Pizzonia
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation - Plaintiff Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
I am originally from Houston Texas, but have lived in New Mexico since 1999. I have represented injured workers against insurance companies since I graduated Law School in 2009. Prior to attending law school at UNM, I graduated from UNM - Anderson School of Management with a dual degree in marketing and operations management. Upon receiving my law degree I immediately began representing injured workers and have done so continuously for a decade.

My passion for representing injured people against insurance companies began when at the age of 21, I was involved in a near fatal accident and suffered catastrophic injuries including collapsed lungs, a lacerated aorta, spinal fractures, and other extensive internal damage. Having fought with insurance companies to cover massive medical bills, I know the frustrations that come with such a life changing event: the helplessness over not being able to work; the uncertainty of not knowing where your next check is coming from; or how you are going to make ends meet, and the pain that you are living with. I have personally experienced it and understand what injured workers go through.

I have been selected to Super Lawyers - Rising Stars list for 4 years running and dedicate myself to my clients. When I am not representing injured workers, I enjoy time with my wife of 17 years, our three children, and our 3 dogs.

attorneys.name: Rikki L. Quintana
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Transactions Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Rikki L. Quintana, who grew up in Santa Fe, New Mexico , earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of New Mexico in 1977, where she was elected to Phi Beta Kappa. She received her Juris Doctor degree from Stanford Law School in 1980, where she was awarded the Franklin Prize in International Law. Ms. Quintana is a member of the State Bars of California and New Mexico , the Albuquerque Bar Association, the New Mexico State Bar Alternative Dispute Resolution Committee, the New Mexico Health Law and Business Law Sections, the New Mexico Defense Lawyers Association and the American Health Lawyers Association. During her career, Ms. Quintana has practiced in the areas of commercial and healthcare business transactions, real estate, corporate law and corporate finance in the Newport Beach, California office of a national law firm, as well as in Albuquerque, New Mexico . She is rated bv by the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory.* Ms. Quintana currently practices in the areas of real estate and commercial business transactions, corporate and non-profit structures, health law, and complex commercial and employment litigation. Her broad practice includes representation of small and medium-sized local and regional businesses, as well as large multi-state companies, in a variety of transactions, including business entity formation; acquisition, financing, development and disposition of real estate, assets and business operations; structuring of health care transactions to comply with federal Stark and anti-kickback laws and New Mexico licensing requirements; and creation and administration of nonprofit organizations. She also devotes a significant portion of her practice to appellate work and briefing dispositive motions in complex civil litigation matters. Ms. Quintana is also a trained mediator.

*The certification was derived from a lawyer poll or survey.

attorneys.name: Shawn Spencer
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiff Personal Injury Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
I joined Parnall Law Firm, LLC, in 2023 with over twenty years of experience helping injured people. I began my legal career defending large corporations but quickly realized I would much rather represent people. I’ve had the opportunity to work with, and against, some of the finest lawyers in the country during my career. Before joining Parnall Law Firm, LLC, I practiced in Oklahoma with a prominent law firm known for helping injured people in auto, tractor-trailer, medical negligence, and class action litigation. Parnall Law Firm, LLC presented me with a new opportunity to join a team with wonderful people, and experienced and talented attorneys, and to continue to help injured people.

I was born and raised in Arkansas in a small rural town in the Arkansas River Valley. My parents and family instilled in me the values of hard work and helping people. I attended the University of Arkansas then attended the University of Arkansas School of Law where I wrote a top paper in my legal research and writing section and participated in Moot Court. After law school, I began practicing law in Fort Smith, Arkansas helping people and small businesses in Oklahoma and Arkansas. I practiced with a respected attorney and quickly gained a lot of experience in trying cases.

My wife, Angela, is a CPA and lifelong educator. We have two wonderful children, Jack and Jamie. We enjoy attending their events and activities and watching them grow.

attorneys.name: Nick Stiver
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Nick grew up in southern New Mexico. He received his undergraduate degree from University of New Mexico. Nick received his law degree from University of New Mexico, School of Law.

Nick started his law career practicing in the areas of personal injury, workers' compensation and social security disability. He knows the interplay between these cases and always tries to get the most compensation for his clients. Since joining Stiver Law, Nick specializes in Workers' Compensation and personal injury. Nick has taken multiple Worker's Compensation cases to trial and won. He has achieved great results for his clients throughout New Mexico.

Work injuries can be very serious and life changing. When Nick gets involved, priority one is to get medical and money benefits started.

Nick takes pride in making sure that the insurance companies treat his clients fairly. Nick has a close, one-on-one partnership with his clients. He is responsive and communicates quickly and efficiently.

When not working, Nick likes to play tennis, go on hikes and spend time with his wife and son. Nick is a sports fan and follows boxing and tennis closely.

"I like to take an aggressive approach to my cases - I believe it is best to move my client's cases forward quickly in order to get a resolution as soon as possible. I want my clients to call, text, or email me if they have any questions. I am happy to help." - Nick Stiver

attorneys.name: Thomas Tedeschi
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in rural Southern Illinois. My parents always stressed to me the importance of public service. I followed their direction by working as a public servant my entire adult life. While in high school and college, I worked at our family’s business. The business consisted of retail paint sales and residential and commercial glass construction. I have served as an Intensive Probation Officer, State’s Attorney Investigator, and Deputy Sheriff. I attended the University of Illinois Police Training Institute in March 1995 and graduated with my basic law enforcement training certification. While at the University of Illinois Police Training Institute, I received the Ervin H. Warren Award (officer who best exemplifies today’s concept of tomorrow’s police officer) and the academic achievement award (highest grade average) for the graduating class. I then aspired to become an attorney, enrolling in law school at Southern Illinois University School of Law, graduating in May 2003.

I served as an Assistant State’s Attorney in Franklin County, Illinois, and prosecuted all levels of criminal cases. In 2008, I was elected Resident Circuit Judge of Franklin County, Illinois. While serving on the bench, I presided over all types of court matters. I conducted approximately 100 jury trials and countless bench trials. I was elected Chief Judge of the Second Judicial Circuit from 2013 to 2021. I am the longest-serving Chief Judge in the history of the Second Judicial Circuit. During my time on the bench, I was appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court to serve on numerous committees and commissions, including the Illinois Pretrial Reform Commission and the Judicial Education Committee. I also served as a New Judge and Peer Judge Mentor, and a Judicial Performance Evaluation facilitator. I retired from the bench on November 30, 2024.

Following retirement, I reflected upon my career and realized I still wished to serve the public. I have enjoyed public service and want to assist individuals in achieving justice when injured. It is a great honor to have a client put their trust in me to help them. I relocated to Albuquerque in June 2025 and love the area and helping my clients here at Parnall Law Firm, LLC. When not working, I enjoy spending time with my wife, Lori Ann. We have four adult children and one grandchild scattered across the United States. We enjoy hiking, fishing, and watching basketball.

I was elected Chief Judge of the Second Judicial Circuit from 2013 to 2021. I am the longest-serving Chief Judge in the history of the Second Judicial Circuit. During my time on the bench, I was appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court to serve on numerous committees and commissions, including the Illinois Pretrial Reform Commission and the Judicial Education Committee. I also served as a New Judge and Peer Judge Mentor, and a Judicial Performance Evaluation facilitator. I retired from the bench on November 30, 2024.

Following retirement, I reflected upon my career and realized I still wished to serve the public. I have enjoyed public service and want to assist individuals in achieving justice when injured. It is a great honor to have a client put their trust in me to help them. I relocated to Albuquerque in June 2025 and love the area and helping my clients here at Parnall Law Firm, LLC. When not working, I enjoy spending time with my wife, Lori Ann. We have four adult children and one grandchild scattered across the United States. We enjoy hiking, fishing, and watching basketball.

attorneys.name: Nicholas J. Trost
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
I have a deep understanding of how insurance companies operate. Before joining Parnall Law, I worked for several years in a law firm that defended insurance companies against claims and actions brought by injured individuals.

With Parnall Law, however, I am using my knowledge to benefit people who have suffered injuries due to the negligence of others.

I grew up in a close-knit Albuquerque family, and my parents and extended family instilled in me the values of hard work and integrity. I attended high school at Bosque School, where the faculty awarded me the Gerald R. Ford Character Award as a senior. The award honors the legacy of President Ford who “followed his conscience despite political cost.” I have been recognized as a Bosque alumni who has continually manifested the school’s core values of Scholarship, Community, and Integrity, through my contributions to my community, career, avocation, education, or causes.

I then headed to Seattle to attend the University of Washington, where I majored in Communications—Journalism, graduating magna cum laude in 2010. As an undergraduate, I worked in the newsroom of KIRO-7 TV, Seattle’s CBS affiliate, and it was there that I decided that I wanted to become a lawyer. At that time, I decided to become a lawyer so I could make a larger, more expansive impression on the world.

After graduation, I returned to my home state to attend the University of New Mexico School of Law, where I served as a member of the New Mexico Law Review and the ABA Moot Court Team. I graduated cum laude in 2013 and began my legal career handling mostly insurance-defense cases as an attorney with an Albuquerque law firm.

I did take some plaintiff’s cases with that firm, however, and I realized I much preferred them. One case in particular made a big impact on me: I represented an individual who was injured after being T-boned in a motor-vehicle accident and I realized that I wanted to use my skills and experience to represent similarly situated individuals against insurance companies and other entities.

When an opportunity arose to join the Parnall Law Team, I jumped at the opportunity. Joining Parnall Law has been one of the highlights of my personal and professional life. I wake up every morning excited to start working. I love fighting for my clients. I love helping them transform their lives after an incident that could have derailed them. I find it so much more rewarding than representing big, rich, faceless, and stingy insurance companies.

During my years in Seattle, I became a passionate fan of the University of Washington Huskies football team and I remain an avid fan today (Go Dawgs). I also enjoy playing golf and spending time with my family. My wife, Quiana, is my rock and my biggest fan. My two (2) girls, Adelina (5), and Paloma (2), are an absolute blessing and teach me so much about life and how we need to appreciate it. My Spanish Water Dog, Cádiz, represents everything that is fun and loving in life.

attorneys.name: Glenn Smith Valdez
attorneys.practice_type: Traffic Violations Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
A New Mexico Traffic Expert

Glenn Smith Valdez is an expert New Mexico Traffic ticket attorney. He has dedicated his practice to representation of drivers accused of a variety of New Mexico traffic violations. He understands the importance of keeping moving violations like speeding, careless driving and the like off his clients' records, and he knows how to make that happen. Glenn also realizes how New Mexico citations affect your insurance rates, and he fights hard to keep your New Mexico citations from costing you money in increased premiums.

An Experienced New Mexico Traffic lawyer

Glenn Smith Valdez is experienced in all facets of New Mexico traffic law. He has represented hundreds of clients and won dismissals for the vast majority. He has dealt with officers of almost every agency in the state, from the New Mexico State Police and New Mexico Department of Transportation officers, to Sheriff's deputies and City officers in every county and almost every city in the state. A great New Mexico traffic attorney, Glenn uses his experience to negotiate dismissals, traffic school, donations in lieu of fines and other diversion programs that keep your New Mexico citation off your record. When you need an experienced New Mexico traffic lawyer, Glenn Smith Valdez is who you need to call.

A New Mexico Traffic Attorney Representing Drivers Statewide

Glenn Smith Valdez has represented drivers ticketed in New Mexico in almost every traffic court in the state. He know the rules and policies for the New Mexico traffic courts and how those rules work to help his clients. When you face a New Mexico traffic charge, you may be unable to appear. Glenn Smith Valdez knows how to waive your appearance. A great New Mexico traffic attorney like Glenn Smith Valdez will file motions to allow you to appear by phone, or motions to allow your attorney to appear for you. Glenn is proud that he has helped hundreds of drivers ticketed in New Mexico get their New Mexico traffic citations dismissed without ever returning to New Mexico or appearing in a New Mexico court.

A New Mexico Traffic Lawyer Lifting Warrants and Suspensions

If you have failed to appear or answer your New Mexico citation or ticket, you may have discovered that you have a New Mexico traffic warrant or you license has been suspended because of your New Mexico ticket. Call Glenn Smith Valdez now. He has experience in resolving New Mexico traffic warrants or bench warrants as well as expertise in reinstating licenses suspended because of New Mexico tickets. He will represent you in New Mexico traffic court and with the New Mexico Motor Vehicle Division. He can help you cancel the New Mexico Warrant with the New Mexico traffic court. He will contact the New Mexico MVD to remove or lift the New Mexico suspension and reinstate your driver's license.

Get Yourself The Best New Mexico Traffic Lawyer

It boils down to this, when you want the best, most experienced New Mexico traffic ticket lawyer, call Glenn Smith Valdez. He has the experience in fighting New Mexico citations and tickets than you need. He can handle any New Mexico traffic matter you have. New Mexico tickets like speeding, careless driving, even reckless driving, suspended licenses and New Mexico traffic warrants – Glenn Smith Valdez can represent in any New Mexico traffic situation. Glenn Smith Valdez will appear for you, fight for you and win for you. If you have a New Mexico traffic ticket, a New Mexico traffic warrant or your license is suspended because of a New Mexico traffic citation, call Glenn Smith Valdez today.

attorneys.name: Ryan J. Villa
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Ryan J. Villa LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Practicing Since 2006

My practice focuses on criminal defense, civil rights, and plaintiff’s personal injury cases. I am licensed to practice law in the State of New Mexico, the United States District Court in the District of New Mexico and the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals. I have conducted dozens of jury trials in federal, state, metropolitan, and various municipal and magistrate courts throughout the State. I have also argued cases in the New Mexico Supreme Court and the Court of Appeals.

I am a native of Albuquerque where I live with my family. I graduated summa cum laude from UNM Law School in 2005. After law school, I clerked for Chief Justice Richard Bosson of the New Mexico Supreme Court from 2005 to 2006. I worked as an attorney with the Robert Cooper Law Firm from 2006 to 2014 before I decided to take the plunge and open my own law firm. Before law school I attended New Mexico State University where I graduated in 2002 with bachelors’ degrees in Criminal Justice and Government with distinction in the University Honors Program. I attended Highland High School here in Albuquerque, graduating in 1998. I am dedicated to trial practice and remain active in the law school community by volunteering to judge and guest coach the UNM mock trial team every year.

The majority of my work involves cases where the government or a large corporate insurance company is the opponent. Whether it be the State or the Federal Government prosecuting a client or a lawsuit against one of these governments or their agents, I take a large measure of pleasure keeping the government and large corporations in line. I have defended clients from all types criminal charges, large and small including DWI, domestic violence, drugs and narcotics—possession and trafficking/sale, white collar crime, and all types of violent crimes including sex offenses and murder. I have also sued all manner of government and governmental agencies, including police departments and police officers for civil rights violations and negligence including the federal government, the State of New Mexico, and several counties and cities. These cases include wrongful death, excessive use of force, illegal arrest, First Amendment violations and gender discrimination. I have also taken on dozens of lawsuits against auto insurance companies and cases involving injuries including premises liability, suits against drunk drivers, dramshop, dog bite, product liability and other injuries. I have handled cases against multi- national, multi-billion dollar corporations on down to small companies who have injured or taken advantage of the unsuspecting person.

I believe that handling a different variety of cases has helped me craft a holistic, well-rounded approach to any case that comes my way. Trying cases in all different courts, criminal and civil, has given me skills that I would not have otherwise gained had I only focused on one area.

attorneys.name: Kelly K. Waterfall
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Ryan J. Villa LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Kelly Waterfall has been an associate with the firm since 2017. Her practice focuses on civil rights and children’s law. She is licensed to practice law in the State of New Mexico and the United States District Court in the District of New Mexico.

Kelly graduated cum laude from the University of New Mexico School of Law in 2005, where she was the recipient of the Jerrold L. Walden Memorial Award, Clinical Honors Award and Bondurant Merit Scholarship. She was also a 2004 Bergstrom Child Welfare Law Fellow. She published the comment State v. Muniz: Authorizing Adult Sentencing of Juveniles Absent a Conviction that Authorizes an Adult Sentence in the New Mexico Law Review, arguing for a change to the New Mexico Delinquency Act that was adopted in 2005.

Kelly began her legal career as a solo practitioner, working as a subcontractor for Pegasus Legal Services for Children to represent children and youth as a guardian ad litem and youth attorney in child welfare and custody matters. She also represented grandparents and other family members in kinship guardianship proceedings. Kelly worked with attorneys at Pegasus Legal Services for Children and other community stakeholders on drafting proposed legislative changes to the Children’s Code, which were adopted in 2007and 2009. She has served on the boards of the Children’s Justice Act Advisory Group and the Children’s Law Section of the State Bar of New Mexico.

In 2010 Kelly began working as an associate at the Law Office of Peter Cubra, representing people with mental disabilities in a federal class action lawsuit and in other civil rights cases in federal court. While part of the Cubra firm she also represented adjudicated delinquent children and youth committed to juvenile facilities in a class action law suit against the New Mexico Children, Youth and Families Department.

Since joining this firm Kelly has continued to represent individuals with mental disabilities in McClendon, Jimmy, et al. v. City of Albuquerque, et al., CV 95-24 JP/KBM. She began working on this case in 2010, participating in all aspects of litigation, settlement negotiations and monitoring of compliance with federal consent decrees. Kelly was also part of a team of attorneys and advocacy organizations that filed and recently settled Kevin S., et al. v. Blalock, et al., CV18-896 KWR/LF. The settlement is designed to improve the treatment of children in New Mexico’s foster care system. For more information about this settlement see: https://kevinssettlement.com/.

Prior to law school Kelly worked and volunteered in the fields of child development and art. She earned her undergraduate degree from the University of Illinois in 1988, where she graduated with University Highest Honors and was awarded the Bronze Tablet. Kelly grew up in Chicago, but has called New Mexico home since 1993.

attorneys.name: Logan Wexler
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiff’s Personal Injury Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
Before joining Parnall Law Firm, LLC, I worked in Personal Injury law for 3 years, handling mostly trucking accidents, pharmaceutical cases, Roundup cases, and premises liability cases. I came to Parnall Law Firm, LLC because I wanted to represent people who are in danger of being mistreated by insurance companies.

I attended the University of Texas School of Law and graduated in 2019. Immediately after graduating, I became a public defender in Albuquerque representing individuals charged with crimes. This practice was meaningful and fulfilling, but I wanted to try personal injury and work alongside my brother, Noah, who has made a career in the business of personal injury law. I found that personal injury was a type of law that I could excel in given the right environment, and Parnall Law Firm, LLC is exactly that.

When you are my client, I will make sure that you are kept informed about the process of your case, and the legal backdrop that will govern the results in your case. It is my honor to educate my clients about insurance companies and defense attorneys, and the tactics they employ as they try to diminish the value of my clients’ cases.

As I learned in my time as a public defender, the process is the punishment. I find that adage to be true for my current clients as well. The headache doesn’t end until the case is over, which can sometimes take months or even years. It’s my job to help my clients navigate all of the problems the legal system will throw at them.

In my spare time, I like to play the piano and produce electronic music.

attorneys.name: Aimee Martuccio Whitsell
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Albuquerque, NM
attorneys.bio:
My name is Aimee Martuccio Whitsell and I am an attorney with Parnall Law Firm, LLC. I come from a big Italian family and was raised in Western Pennsylvania with my four sisters. My dad continued the paving company his dad started after immigrating to the United States, and he was able to put all of his daughters through college.

I graduated from Westminster College cum laude with a double major in Philosophy and History in 2001. For some reason, I have been fascinated by the history of the “Old West” since childhood…especially Billy the Kid. As a self-proclaimed Billy the Kid aficionado, I eagerly moved to New Mexico for law school in 2001. While in law school, I served as an officer for the Veteran’s Association, completed an internship with the Second Judicial District Attorney’s Office, and worked in the Southwest Indian Law Clinic.

After graduating from law school in 2004, I started my career as a Children’s Court prosecutor for the Thirteenth Judicial District Attorney for three years. While a prosecutor, I obtained valuable trial experience, including lead chair in jury trials of high-profile felonies.

I began my civil law practice in 2008 with a focus in medical malpractice defense, and I also worked for a large national medical malpractice insurance company. In 2017, I changed my path and now I represent individuals injured by negligence. I have now been on almost every side of a case – defense attorney, insurance representative, and now plaintiff advocate. I use my unique background and skills to even the playing field for individuals battling for their rights against big corporations and insurance companies. I have insight into the motives behind opposing counsel’s strategies and can anticipate their arguments and tactics.

My family has always been my greatest joy and motivator. Parnall Law Firm, LLC is like my second home. We have the values, compassion, and skills necessary to truly help our community. I am proud of the work we do every day.

“All of my clients’ cases are important, big or small. We can’t undo the injury or trauma they have gone through, but we can help them get back on their feet and obtain a sense of justice. Helping clients obtain just compensation is the best and only form of justice when they are wrongly harmed by another’s negligence.”

attorneys.bio:
James Wood played football for his father, legendary high school football coach, Gordon Wood. Jim brings the grit, competitive spirit, and enthusiasm he learned on the gridiron with him every time he enters the courtroom. "All we ask for is a level playing field", Jim says. Concern for other people is the reason Jim is a trial lawyer: Helping people find justice is the most satisfying part of the work we do at the Wood Law Firm. When the strong injure the weak or greed overcomes fairness, Jim takes it personally. Behind every case, there is someone, often many people, who suffered, people whose lives changed. You can never forget that fact.

Jim and his wife, Jan, are proud parents of two wonderful children, Ty and Erin. Jim served as Chair of the Randall County Democratic Party from 1996 through 2003. Jim is an avid horseman and a member of the National Cutting Horse Association and the American Quarter Horse Association.
